harm_plain: Birds spread its berries into woodlands, where it forms thick spiny patches that crowd out native shrubs and wildflowers.
Birds carry its seeds into forests, where it shades out native plants on the forest floor.
Escapes from gardens and forms thick mats on the forest floor that smother native wildflowers.
Forms dense walls of reeds in wetlands and ditches that push out native plants and wildlife habitat. Its tall dry stalks build up over winter.
Its heavy shade and shallow roots stop native trees and wildflowers from growing underneath, and its seeds spread into nearby forests.
Spreads fast over open land and roadsides, crowds out native plants, and its seeds last in the soil for decades.
Climbs and smothers trees and covers the forest floor so native plants can't grow; heavy vines can bring trees down.
Forms huge thorny thickets along streams and edges that push out native plants and block access.
